title: Cu Chulainn and Ferdiad at the Ford
text:
Cu Chulainn and Ferdiad had trained together as youths under the warrior woman Scathach. They were foster brothers in arms and had sworn friendship. But when Queen Medb of Connacht invaded Ulster in the Cattle Raid of Cooley, Cu Chulainn alone held the fords against her army, and Medb, running out of champions, turned to Ferdiad. With rich gifts, her daughter's hand and the threat that her poets would shame him with satire, she persuaded him to fight his friend.

The two met at a ford and fought for three days. Each evening, when the fighting stopped, they threw their arms around each other and kissed. Their horses shared a paddock and their charioteers a fire. Cu Chulainn sent Ferdiad healing herbs for his wounds, and Ferdiad sent Cu Chulainn a share of his food.

On the fourth day the fighting turned desperate. When Ferdiad gained the upper hand, Cu Chulainn called for the gae bolga, his terrible barbed spear, and with it struck Ferdiad a mortal blow.

Cu Chulainn carried his friend's body across the ford to the Ulster side, then collapsed beside it. He grieved over him in a famous lament, crying that all the fighting before had been play compared to this. The ford was named after Ferdiad.
lesson: Do not let others turn you against a friend with bribes or pressure. Even in real disagreement, you can keep respect and decency toward the people you care about.
source: Tain Bo Cuailnge (The Cattle Raid of Cooley), Book of Leinster recension
